item.title: Meduza: Moscow police call a weekend sweep of hundreds of young people a ‘preventive measure.’ Detainees report beatings, military summonses, and pressure to sign army contracts.
item.description: On the evening of November 7, police carried out a mass roundup in Moscow’s Kitai-Gorod neighborhood. By the most widely cited estimates, 150 to 200 people were detained in total (though some reports put the number at 300), most of them young people, including minors. It was a planned raid: around 8 p.m., 10 police vans pulled up to Gorka Park on Bolshoi Spasoglinishchevsky Lane, and police loaded young people into them. Eyewitnesses said police were rounding up “anyone and everyone.”

item.title: Meduza: Drug-resistant infections put wounded Ukrainian soldiers at risk of amputation. Doctors are trying to help by treating them like victims of a biological attack.
item.description: In late October, The New York Times published a report on how doctors are helping Ukrainian soldiers fight antibiotic-resistant infections. Correspondent Marc Santora traveled to Dnipro and Poland, spoke with doctors and patients, and joined science reporter Gina Kolata to examine the problem and a potential solution. Here, we summarize their reporting alongside additional details from the participating doctors’ interviews, presentations, and scientific papers.
